learn.title: Database and unstructured data migration
objectives: Choose a SQL Server migration method (Managed Instance link, Log Replay Service, native backup and restore, Azure Database Migration Service, transactional replication, BACPAC) based on target, downtime and source version

Use current tooling: SQL Server migration in Azure Arc and Azure Migrate for assessment, and Azure DMS in the portal, PowerShell or Azure CLI. Azure Data Studio, its migration extension and Data Migration Assistant are retired
Migrate open-source and NoSQL databases: the migration service in Azure Database for PostgreSQL, DMS for MySQL, and the Azure DocumentDB migration extension for MongoDB
Pick an unstructured data tool: AzCopy, Azure Storage Explorer, Azure Storage Mover, Azure File Sync, Azure Data Factory, Azure Data Box, Data Box Disk and Import/Export
Use bandwidth and time maths to decide between online (network) and offline (shipped device) transfer, and combine offline seeding with online delta sync
concepts: Online vs offline migration

Offline: applications stop and the data is copied, so downtime lasts as long as the copy. Online: the source stays in use while an initial copy is followed by continuous change replication, and downtime is only the short cutover.
Managed Instance link

Uses distributed availability groups to replicate SQL Server databases to Azure SQL Managed Instance in near real time. The target is readable during migration, there is no time limit before cutover, and it suits Business Critical targets. Sources are SQL Server 2016 and later (Enterprise, Standard or Developer).
Log Replay Service (LRS)

Based on log shipping. You upload full, differential and log backups to Azure Blob Storage and LRS restores them continuously to SQL Managed Instance. It works with older SQL Server versions and all editions and uses a public endpoint. Databases can't be read until cutover, and it isn't recommended for Business Critical targets.
SQL Server migration in Azure Arc

For SQL Server instances enabled by Azure Arc: a free assessment runs automatically every week, gives readiness and sizing, and you can migrate from the Azure portal to SQL Managed Instance (MI link or LRS), SQL Server on Azure VMs or Azure SQL Database (preview). It replaces the retired Azure Data Studio migration extension.
Azure Database Migration Service

Fully managed service available in the Azure portal, PowerShell and Azure CLI. Supports online and offline migration to SQL Managed Instance and SQL Server on Azure VMs, and offline migration to Azure SQL Database (schema and data, using a self-hosted integration runtime).
Native backup and restore

Back up SQL Server to URL (.bak files in Blob Storage) and restore to SQL Managed Instance or SQL Server on an Azure VM. Simple, but downtime covers the full backup, copy and restore. Azure SQL Database can't restore native .bak files.
Transactional replication

Publisher-subscriber replication of tables. It can keep Azure SQL Database or SQL Managed Instance in sync as a subscriber for a minimal-downtime cutover, or migrate only a subset of tables. Setup is more complex than other options.
BACPAC / SqlPackage

A .bacpac file holds a database's schema and data. You export it from the source and import it to Azure SQL Database or SQL Managed Instance. Needs downtime, so it suits smaller databases. Use SqlPackage for scale.
PostgreSQL migration service

Built into Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server (portal or CLI). Migrates schema and data from on-premises, Azure VMs, Amazon RDS, Aurora and Google Cloud SQL, online or offline. Online mode requires primary keys on all tables.
Azure Storage Mover

Fully managed file and object migration with one resource to manage many shares. Usually an agent VM runs near the source (there are also agentless SMB options). Handles SMB and NFS shares and AWS S3 to Azure Files or Blob, and can do repeated incremental copies, so it fits the delta sync after a Data Box seed.
Azure Data Box family

Shipped devices for offline transfer. Data Box Disk: up to 5 x 8 TB SSDs, about 35 TB usable per order, import only. Data Box (next generation): 120 TB or 525 TB usable, import and export. Data Box Heavy is retired. Import/Export lets you ship your own drives.
Bandwidth maths

1 Gbps is about 125 MB/s, or about 10.8 TB per day at full use. 100 Mbps is about 1.08 TB per day. Divide data size by usable daily throughput (after the share you can use), then compare with the deadline to choose online or offline.
comparisons: MI link: near real-time, readable target, best for minimal downtime and Business Critical, SQL Server 2016 and later, needs network connectivity between SQL Server and the managed instance. LRS: backup-based, works with all editions and older versions, public endpoint, target not readable, best for General Purpose when some downtime is OK.
Target: Managed Instance vs Azure SQL Database vs Azure VM

Managed Instance accepts native backups, LRS and MI link. Azure SQL Database needs a logical migration (DMS offline, BACPAC, transactional replication). SQL Server on an Azure VM accepts anything SQL Server accepts, plus DMS online and offline.
AzCopy vs Storage Explorer vs Storage Mover

AzCopy: scriptable command line for one-off or small to medium jobs and server-to-server copies. Storage Explorer: a GUI for occasional manual work. Storage Mover: managed, at-scale share migration (typically more than 1 TB or millions of files) with central oversight.
Azure File Sync vs Storage Mover

Azure File Sync keeps Windows file servers in continuous sync with Azure file shares and offers cloud tiering (hybrid, ongoing). Storage Mover is a migration service that moves the data and lets you retire the source, and it also supports NFS and S3 sources.
Online network transfer vs Data Box

Use the network when the maths fits the deadline and the link can be spared. Use Data Box when data is large (tens of TB or more) and bandwidth is limited or missing. For active data, seed with Data Box and then catch up the changes online.
Data Box Disk vs Data Box vs Import/Export

Data Box Disk: small orders up to about 35 TB, USB/SATA, import only. Data Box: 120 or 525 TB, import and export, data copy service. Import/Export: your own drives, import to Blob or Files, export from Blob only.
traps: Azure Data Studio, its Azure SQL migration extension (retired February 28, 2026) and Data Migration Assistant (retired July 2025) are not current answers. Use Azure Arc, Azure Migrate or Azure DMS.
Azure SQL Database can't restore native .bak files, and MI link and LRS only target SQL Managed Instance. For minimal downtime to SQL Database, think transactional replication.
With LRS, databases stay in restoring mode until cutover. If the target must be readable during migration, choose MI link.
Data Box Disk is import only and Data Box Heavy is retired. For export or very large transfers, use Data Box.
Watch the units: Mbps and Gbps are bits, file sizes are bytes. Divide by 8, and reduce for the share of the link you can actually use.
An online migration only finishes when you cut over (for example the DocumentDB extension and MI link). Watch replication lag before you cut over.
revision: Minimal downtime to SQL Managed Instance with a readable target: MI link. Older version or all editions with some downtime: LRS. Simplest: native backup to URL.
For SQL Server enabled by Azure Arc, the portal's Database migration pane assesses for free every week and migrates to SQL Managed Instance with MI link or LRS.
DMS (portal, PowerShell, CLI): online and offline to SQL Managed Instance and SQL Server on Azure VMs, offline to Azure SQL Database.

PostgreSQL: use the migration service in flexible server (online mode needs primary keys). MySQL: DMS (online needs ROW binlog format). MongoDB to Azure DocumentDB: VS Code migration extension (online mode needs change streams).

Files: AzCopy for scripted one-off jobs, Storage Explorer for GUI work, Storage Mover for managed migrations at scale, Azure File Sync for hybrid sync with cloud tiering, Data Factory for orchestrated pipelines.
Offline: Data Box Disk up to about 35 TB, Data Box 120 or 525 TB (import and export), Import/Export with your own drives.
1 Gbps is about 10.8 TB per day. If data size divided by usable TB per day is more than the deadline, ship a Data Box. Then use Storage Mover for the changes.
